content: Solanum nigrum, commonly known as Black Nightshade, Duscle, Garden Nightshade, Hound's Berry, Petty Morel, Small-fruited Black Nightshade, Sunberry, or Wonderberry, is a plant species belonging to the Solanum genus. It is native to Eurasia but has also been introduced to the Americas. In Hawaii, it is referred to as popolo. The green berries and mature leaves of this plant contain glycoalkaloids, which are toxic when consumed raw. The level of toxicity varies among different strains, and some strains produce berries that are safe to eat when fully ripe. Historically, this plant has been used for medicinal purposes, with its usage dating back to ancient Greece. Black Nightshade is a relatively common plant that grows in various wooded areas and disturbed habitats. Its leaves are approximately 5 cm long, ovate to heart-shaped, and have wavy or large-toothed edges. The flowers of the plant feature petals that are greenish to whitish in color, which become recurved as they age, and they surround prominent bright yellow anthers. The fruits are oval-shaped black berries that grow in small, hanging clusters.
